evals.name: first-time-bootstrap
evals.prompt: I just started with ConfigHub. Can you set up some example Units I can poke at?
evals.expected_output: Creates the skill-examples Space, scaffolds hello-ns and hello-app Units via kubectl dry-run, applies the defaults-function chain on each Unit with --change-desc carrying the user prompt, and finishes by pointing the user at the GUI (--web) and suggesting a specific next skill to try (e.g., cub-mutate or cub-query).

evals.name: idempotent-rerun
evals.prompt: The skill-examples space already exists but I want to make sure everything is in the right state. Can you re-run the setup?
evals.expected_output: Detects that the Space and Units already exist (cub space get, cub unit list), skips create steps, re-runs the defaults functions (which are hermetic + idempotent) without producing noisy no-op revisions, and reports the current state plainly. Does not delete or recreate anything.

evals.name: walk-through-example
evals.prompt: Walk me through ConfigHub with a real example I can see end to end.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bootstrap, then narrates what happened in plain English — Space created, Units seeded, defaults applied via functions (each with --change-desc), revision history shows provenance — and offers clickable trust URLs (cub unit get --web, cub revision list --web) so the user can see the outcome in the GUI. Does not dump YAML inline when a --web link would do.
